001import javafx.scene.media.Media;
002import javafx.scene.media.MediaPlayer;
003import java.io.File;
004import javafx.application.Application;
005import javafx.stage.Stage;
006import java.util.Scanner;
007import javafx.scene.control.Label;
008
009/**
010 * 
011 * Holds the song player that plays media for the jukebox 
012 * 
013 * @author Jason Jiang
014 * @version 1.0
015 * */
016// This java class is only a helpful class meant to be held by a running program
017public class SongPlayer{
018    Media song;
019    MediaPlayer mediaPlayer;
020    purchaseQueue queue;
021    Label nowPlayingLabel;
022    Boolean isPlaying = false;
023    String songName;
024    /**Plays songs from queue when asked 
025     * @param q the queue we are pulling from
026     * @param l the label that is our outputting the status messages
027    */
028
029    public SongPlayer(purchaseQueue q, Label l){
030        this.queue = q;
031        nowPlayingLabel = l;
032    }
033    
034// Idea of using callback to generate media players over and over inspired by 
035// stack overflow questionns 61296959
036/**
037 * This function gets run when the media is done playing, tries to play the next song on the queue
038 * 
039 */
040    public void endOfMediaNextSong(){
041        System.out.println("Finished song");
042        if (queue.getQueueSize() > 0){
043        System.out.println("Sng Start");
044            
045            popQueuePlaySong();
046        }else{
047            isPlaying = false;
048            nowPlayingLabel.setText("End of Queue Thank you.");
049
050            if (mediaPlayer != null){
051            mediaPlayer.dispose();
052            }
053        }
054        }
055// not learned in class yet, the double colon operator, in the case of [A]::[B]
056// point at the method B in class A.
057// This is a callback funnction, so when the media player is over, it can call that function and boom new song.
058        
059    
060/**
061 * This attempts to start playing from the queue, but only if the media is not already playing
062 * @return boolean, wether it was successful in starting the media playing from queue.
063 */
064    public boolean start_queue(){
065        if (!isPlaying && queue.getQueueSize() >0){
066            popQueuePlaySong();
067            return true;
068        }
069        return false;
070    }
071
072/**This is the main way this player plays media, and updates the ui to show that media is playing.
073 * 
074 * @return weather its playing or not
075 */
076    public boolean popQueuePlaySong(){
077        isPlaying = true;
078        if (mediaPlayer != null){
079            mediaPlayer.dispose();
080        }
081        String x = queue.nextSong().toString();
082        nowPlayingLabel.setText("Now Playing: "+queue.getPlayingSongName()+"\n" + queue.displayQueue());
083        System.out.println("Playing next song: "+x);
084        song = new Media(x);
085        mediaPlayer = new MediaPlayer(song);
086        mediaPlayer.setAutoPlay(true);
087        mediaPlayer.play();
088        mediaPlayer.setOnEndOfMedia(this::endOfMediaNextSong);
089        System.out.println(queue.displayQueue());
090        return true;
091    }
092}
